topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session's themes and outlines the learning outcomes regarding cellular transformation and cancer genetics.

topics.label: Tumor virology and cellular transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the discovery of transforming viruses led to the identification of cellular proto-oncogenes and established laboratory assays to measure malignant transformation.

topics.label: Cancer gene classifications, allele dosage, and pathway regulation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how oncogenic and tumor-suppressive mutations alter cell cycle control and dictate cellular phenotypes based on allele dosage and mutation type.

topics.label: Mechanisms and cellular consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the molecular defects in DNA repair, replication, and mitosis that generate sequence and chromosomal instability, along with their physiological impacts on cancer cells.

topics.label: Multi-step tumor progression and hereditary cancer predispositions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address how the stepwise accumulation of somatic mutations drives cancer evolution and how inherited germline mutations accelerate this progression.

topics.label: Conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session and provides recommended reading material.
